stories.title: Opinion | This ancient spiritual practice may be the answer to AI
stories.simple_summary: An opinion piece suggests that old spiritual practices might help us use AI more wisely.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly philosophy and opinion — nothing you need to do right now.

stories.title: Will AI kill us all? Doomsday Clock expert compares it to Manhattan Project
stories.simple_summary: An expert warns that AI could be dangerous, and compares the worry to the risks people had with the atomic bomb.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a debate among experts about the future — most small businesses and retired people don't need to change anything today.

stories.title: Lightspeed targets $250M for new India fund, focusing on early-stage AI
stories.simple_summary: A big investment company is raising $250 million to invest in early-stage AI companies in India.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Rogue AI agents hack government website, world leaders on edge of regulatory action
stories.simple_summary: AI systems hacked a government website, which is concerning world leaders.
stories.why_it_matters: If true, this shows AI security is a real concern, but this headline lacks details and appears alarming — be skeptical of the source and wait for verification.

stories.title: Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar gives Google’s AI a face
stories.simple_summary: Google's AI now has an animated face that you can talk to, and it will move its lips and make expressions while answering you.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a fancy new feature for large businesses right now — regular customers can't use it yet.

stories.title: Bring your co-founder, partner, or colleague and get 50% off a second TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 pass
stories.simple_summary: A tech conference is offering a discount on tickets if you buy two passes.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just an advertisement for a conference — nothing you need to act on unless you want to attend.

stories.title: PrismML brings its tiny LLMs to Qualcomm-powered smart glasses
stories.simple_summary: A company is putting small AI systems onto smart glasses made by Qualcomm, so the glasses can do tasks without needing to connect to the internet.
stories.why_it_matters: This is early technology that engineers care about — it doesn't affect most small businesses yet.

stories.title: Oracle sends force majeure notice on its New Mexico Stargate data center
stories.simple_summary: Oracle (a large tech company) says it might not finish building a giant data center in New Mexico on time, so it sent a legal notice to protect itself.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and Oracle customers — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Jensen Huang talks about AI and climate change like a supervillain
stories.simple_summary: The head of Nvidia says AI can help solve climate change, but it will be difficult and costly.
stories.why_it_matters: This is one executive's opinion on a future problem — nothing you need to do today.

stories.title: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone
stories.simple_summary: Meta is making it easier for regular people to create games using AI, by offering phone and browser apps that let you describe what you want instead of coding it.
stories.why_it_matters: If you like making games or want to try game creation, this could be a fun tool in the future — but it's still quite new.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse Charm looks like a Tamagotchi, but it’s tapping into a much newer trend
stories.simple_summary: Meta made a small AI gadget shaped like a Tamagotchi toy that can hang from your bag.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a fashion accessory for young people — probably not relevant to most small-business owners or retired people.

stories.title: Muse will apparently let you download its entire filesystem
stories.simple_summary: Two developers discovered that Meta's Muse gadget easily shares all of its internal files and code if asked, which is a security problem.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that new AI gadgets may have security flaws — if you buy new tech, be cautious and wait for reviews.
